events.title: First recorded editorial peer review
events.text: Henry Oldenburg, founding editor of Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society, left the first record of editorial review of manuscripts before publication.
events.quote: The first record of an editorial pre-publication peer-review is from 1665 by Henry Oldenburg

events.title: First scientific journal appears in Paris
events.text: The Journal des sçavans, founded by Denis de Sallo, published its first issue; it is regarded as the earliest scientific journal.
events.quote: The first issue appeared as a twelve-page quarto pamphlet on Monday, 5 January 1665.

events.title: Arbuthnot's early significance test on birth records
events.text: John Arbuthnot analysed 82 years of London birth records; his reasoning is credited as the first use of significance tests.
events.quote: John Arbuthnot studied this question in 1710

events.title: James Lind's controlled scurvy experiment
events.text: Ship surgeon James Lind compared several dietary treatments for scurvy in twelve sailors, one of the first controlled clinical experiments; citrus fruit gave the best results.
events.quote: This was carried out from 20 May 1747 with twelve patients

events.title: Bayes' essay on inverse probability presented
events.text: Thomas Bayes's posthumous essay, edited by Richard Price, was read aloud at the Royal Society; it contains a special case of Bayes' theorem.
events.quote: read it aloud at the Royal Society on 23 December 1763

events.title: Laplace independently develops Bayesian reasoning
events.text: Pierre-Simon Laplace reproduced and extended Bayes's results without knowing of Bayes's work; the Bayesian interpretation of probability was developed mainly by Laplace.
events.quote: He reproduced and extended Bayes's results in 1774

events.title: Peirce describes the 'weight of evidence'
events.text: Charles Sanders Peirce used the logarithm of the factor in the odds form of Bayes' theorem, now called the Bayes factor, as the weight of evidence.
events.quote: In 1878, Charles Sanders Peirce used the logarithm of this factor

events.title: Karl Pearson pools typhoid inoculation studies
events.text: Karl Pearson collated data from several studies of typhoid inoculation in the British Medical Journal, seen as the first use of a meta-analytic approach.
events.quote: a 1904 paper by the statistician Karl Pearson published in the British Medical Journal collated data from several studies of typhoid inoculation

events.title: Fisher's Statistical Methods for Research Workers
events.text: In this influential book Ronald Fisher popularised significance tests and proposed p = 0.05 as a limit for statistical significance.
events.quote: In his highly influential book Statistical Methods for Research Workers (1925), Fisher proposed the level p = 0.05

events.title: Neyman and Pearson publish their lemma
events.text: Jerzy Neyman and Egon Pearson published the Neyman–Pearson lemma, showing how to construct most powerful tests with a fixed Type I error rate.
events.quote: It was introduced by Jerzy Neyman and Egon Pearson in a paper in 1933.

events.title: Jeffreys publishes Theory of Probability
events.text: Harold Jeffreys's book played an important role in the revival of the objective Bayesian view of probability.
events.quote: His book, Theory of Probability, which was first published in 1939

events.title: Sensitivity and specificity introduced
events.text: Biostatistician Jacob Yerushalmy introduced the terms sensitivity and specificity, the basic measures for reporting the accuracy of diagnostic tests.
events.quote: were introduced by American biostatistician Jacob Yerushalmy in 1947

events.title: Nuremberg Code formulated in Doctors' Trial
events.text: The judges in the Nuremberg Doctors' Trial delivered their verdict; its ten points, including voluntary informed consent, became known as the Nuremberg Code.
events.quote: On 20 August 1947, the judges delivered their verdict against Karl Brandt and 22 others.

events.title: First published randomised controlled trial in medicine
events.text: A Medical Research Council trial of streptomycin for pulmonary tuberculosis became the first published randomised controlled trial in medicine.
events.quote: The first published Randomized Controlled Trial in medicine appeared in the 1948 paper entitled

events.title: Framingham Heart Study begins
events.text: The Framingham Heart Study started following 5,209 adults; it became the source of the term risk factor.
events.quote: The study began in 1948 with 5,209 adult subjects from Framingham

events.title: Meehl's Clinical vs. Statistical Prediction
events.text: Paul Meehl argued that mechanical, algorithmic methods of combining data predict behaviour better than clinical judgement, a controversial conclusion later supported by meta-analyses.
events.quote: Meehl's 1954 book Clinical vs. Statistical Prediction

events.title: Lindley names the Bayesian–frequentist paradox
events.text: Dennis Lindley called the disagreement between Bayesian and frequentist tests of the same hypothesis a paradox; Jeffreys had already discussed it in 1939.
events.quote: after Dennis Lindley called the disagreement a paradox in a 1957 paper

events.title: Open peer commentary begins in Current Anthropology
events.text: Anthropologist Sol Tax founded Current Anthropology, which published signed expert commentaries alongside articles together with the authors' replies.
events.quote: Open peer commentary was first implemented by the anthropologist Sol Tax, who founded the journal Current Anthropology in 1957.

events.title: Publication bias first described
events.text: Statistician Theodore Sterling first discussed how studies with successful results are more likely to be published than others.
events.quote: The subject was first discussed in 1959 by statistician Theodore Sterling

events.title: Low statistical power in psychology first noted
events.text: From 1962 onward it was repeatedly pointed out that most psychological studies have low statistical power, a problem that persisted for about fifty years.
events.quote: It had been repeatedly pointed out since 1962 that most psychological studies have low power

events.title: Science Citation Index launched
events.text: Eugene Garfield's Institute for Scientific Information launched the Science Citation Index, which became available online in 1997 under its current name.
events.quote: launched in 1964 as Science Citation Index (SCI)

events.title: Declaration of Helsinki adopted
events.text: The World Medical Association adopted a set of ethical principles for medical research involving human participants, later revised several times.
events.quote: The Declaration was originally adopted in June 1964 in Helsinki, Finland

events.title: Archie Cochrane's Effectiveness and Efficiency
events.text: Archie Cochrane published a book describing the lack of controlled trials behind many accepted medical practices, inspiring later systematic reviews.
events.quote: In 1972, Archie Cochrane published Effectiveness and Efficiency, which described the lack of controlled trials supporting many practices that had previously been assumed to be effective.

events.title: Tuskegee syphilis study exposed
events.text: Press reports exposed the US Public Health Service study of untreated syphilis in African American men, which had run since 1932; the study was then ended.
events.quote: The story broke first in the Washington Star on July 25, 1972

events.title: Journal impact factors calculated yearly
events.text: Impact factors, devised by Eugene Garfield, began to be calculated every year for journals listed in the Journal Citation Reports.
events.quote: Impact factors began to be calculated yearly starting from 1975 for journals listed in the Journal Citation Reports (JCR).

events.title: The term meta-analysis is coined
events.text: Statistician Gene V. Glass coined the term meta-analysis for the statistical analysis of results from many studies.
events.quote: was coined in 1976 by the statistician Gene V

events.title: Belmont Report released
events.text: A US national commission released the Belmont Report, setting out ethical principles and guidelines for the protection of human subjects of research.
events.quote: On September 30, 1978, the commission's report, Ethical Principles and Guidelines for the Protection of Human Subjects of Research, was released.

events.title: The file drawer problem named
events.text: Psychologist Robert Rosenthal coined the term file drawer problem for studies with null results that remain unpublished.
events.quote: was coined by psychologist Robert Rosenthal in 1979

events.title: First APACHE intensive care score
events.text: Knaus and colleagues presented the first APACHE model, a score that estimates severity of disease and risk of death in intensive care patients.
events.quote: The first APACHE model was presented by Knaus et al. in 1981.

events.title: The term evidence-based medicine introduced
events.text: Gordon Guyatt introduced the term evidence-based medicine in an editorial, naming an approach that bases clinical decisions on critically appraised research.
events.quote: a term first formally introduced in a 1991 editorial in the ACP Journal Club

events.title: US Common Rule for human subjects
events.text: Fourteen US federal departments and agencies joined the Department of Health and Human Services in adopting a uniform set of rules for protecting human research subjects.
events.quote: In 1991, 14 other federal departments and agencies joined HHS in adopting a uniform set of rules for the protection of human subjects

events.title: arXiv preprint server starts
events.text: Paul Ginsparg created a central repository for physics preprints at Los Alamos National Laboratory, which grew into the arXiv.
events.quote: Begun on August 14, 1991

events.title: Ottawa ankle rules published
events.text: Emergency doctors in Ottawa published a set of rules to help decide which patients with ankle or foot pain need an X-ray for a possible fracture.
events.quote: This list of rules was published in 1992 by a team of doctors in the emergency department of the Ottawa Civic Hospital in Ottawa, Canada.

events.title: Office of Research Integrity created in the US
events.text: The US Office of Research Integrity was formed by merging two federal offices that oversaw scientific misconduct investigations in Public Health Service-funded research.
events.quote: merged in May 1992

events.title: Cochrane Collaboration founded
events.text: The Cochrane Collaboration was founded under the leadership of Iain Chalmers to produce systematic reviews of health care evidence.
events.quote: was founded in 1993 under the leadership of Iain Chalmers

events.title: First CONSORT Statement
events.text: Journal editors, trialists and methodologists published the CONSORT Statement, a consensus checklist for reporting randomised trials, merging two earlier proposals.
events.quote: This resulted in the Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) Statement, which was first published in 1996.

events.title: Bermuda Principles on genome data release
events.text: Leaders of the Human Genome Project agreed that all DNA sequence data should be released in public databases within 24 hours of generation.
events.quote: At a 1996 summit in Bermuda, leaders of the scientific community agreed on a groundbreaking set of principles

events.title: Sokal hoax in Social Text
events.text: Physicist Alan Sokal had a nonsense article published in the cultural studies journal Social Text and then revealed it as a hoax.
events.quote: Three weeks after its publication in May 1996, Sokal revealed in the magazine Lingua Franca that the article was a hoax.

events.title: Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) founded
events.text: A small group of medical journal editors in the United Kingdom established COPE, which later issued guidance and a code of conduct for journal editors.
events.quote: COPE was established in 1997 by a small group of medical journal editors in the United Kingdom.

events.title: Original Framingham Risk Score published
events.text: The first Framingham Risk Score, a model predicting individual risk of coronary heart disease, was published; updated versions followed in 2002 and 2008.
events.quote: The original Framingham Risk Score had been published in 1998.

events.title: BMJ moves to open peer review
events.text: The British Medical Journal began revealing reviewers' identities to authors, one of the first large journals to do so.
events.quote: Also in 1999, the British Medical Journal moved to an open peer review system

events.title: Dutch law on medical research takes effect
events.text: The Dutch Medical Research Involving Human Subjects Act (WMO) came into force, with the CCMO installed to oversee review of research with human participants.
events.quote: op 1 april 1999 treedt de Wet medisch-wetenschappelijk onderzoek met mensen in werking

events.title: GRADE working group begins
events.text: Methodologists, guideline developers and clinicians began the GRADE collaboration to rate the certainty of evidence and strength of recommendations.
events.quote: The GRADE began in the year 2000 as a collaboration of methodologists

events.title: Public Library of Science founded
events.text: PLOS began as a petition for free access to research articles and became a nonprofit open access publisher; PLOS Biology appeared in 2003.
events.quote: It was founded in 2000 and launched its first journal, PLOS Biology, on October 13, 2003.

events.title: ClinicalTrials.gov opens to the public
events.text: The US National Library of Medicine launched ClinicalTrials.gov, a public trial registry required by the FDA Modernization Act of 1997.
events.quote: made ClinicalTrials.gov available to the public via the internet on February 29, 2000

events.title: EU Clinical Trials Directive adopted
events.text: The European Union adopted Directive 2001/20/EC to harmonise rules and good clinical practice for trials of medicinal products in member states.
events.quote: Directive 2001/20/EC of 4 April 2001

events.title: Budapest Open Access Initiative
events.text: A statement of principles arising from a 2001 meeting in Budapest gave one of the first widely used definitions of open access.
events.quote: which was released to the public on February 14, 2002

events.title: Bell Labs report on Jan Hendrik Schön
events.text: A Bell Labs investigating committee publicly released its report on physicist Jan Hendrik Schön; journals including Science and Nature later withdrew many of his articles.
events.quote: On September 25, 2002, the committee released its report publicly.

events.title: Berlin Declaration on Open Access
events.text: Following a conference of the Max Planck Society, research organisations signed a declaration supporting open access to knowledge.
events.quote: The statement itself was published on October 22, 2003.

events.title: OECD declaration on publicly funded data
events.text: Science ministers of OECD countries declared that publicly funded archive data should be made publicly available; OECD guidelines followed in 2007.
events.quote: In 2004, the Science Ministers of all nations of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)

events.title: Elsevier launches Scopus
events.text: The publisher Elsevier launched Scopus, an abstract and citation database, as a competitor to Web of Science.
events.quote: launched by the academic publisher Elsevier as a competitor to older Web of Science in 2004

events.title: Lawsuit over withheld paroxetine trial data
events.text: New York State Attorney General Eliot Spitzer sued GlaxoSmithKline for withholding clinical trial data on paroxetine in adolescents, including from Study 329.
events.quote: In June 2004 New York State Attorney Eliot Spitzer filed a lawsuit against GSK

events.title: Medical journal editors require trial registration
events.text: Editors of leading medical journals announced they would only publish trials registered in a public registry from the start.
events.quote: In September 2004, editors of prominent medical journals

events.title: Rofecoxib (Vioxx) withdrawn worldwide
events.text: Merck withdrew rofecoxib after its own trial showed increased cardiovascular risk; disclosures followed that risk information had been withheld for years.
events.quote: Merck publicly announced its voluntary withdrawal of the drug from the market worldwide on September 30, 2004.

events.title: Google Scholar released
events.text: Google Scholar was released in beta, indexing journals, books, theses, preprints and other scholarly literature.
events.quote: Released in beta in November 2004

events.title: Ioannidis: 'Why Most Published Research Findings Are False'
events.text: John Ioannidis published an essay in PLOS Medicine arguing that most published research findings are false; it is considered foundational to metascience.
events.quote: is a 2005 essay written by John Ioannidis

events.title: DANS founded
events.text: The Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) and the Dutch Research Council (NWO) founded DANS, a national centre for archiving and reusing research data.
events.quote: DANS is opgericht in 2005 door de Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie van Wetenschappen (KNAW) en de Nederlandse Organisatie voor Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek (NWO).

events.title: Dutch code of conduct on research integrity
events.text: A Dutch code of conduct on research integrity was introduced, setting out standards for scientific practice in the Netherlands.
events.quote: the Dutch code of conduct on research integrity, introduced in 2005

events.title: h-index proposed by Jorge Hirsch
events.text: Physicist Jorge E. Hirsch suggested the h-index as a single number to characterise a researcher's publications and citations.
events.quote: The index was suggested in 2005 by Jorge E. Hirsch

events.title: Dutch universities launch DAREnet
events.text: Sixteen Dutch universities jointly launched DAREnet, an open repository network with over 47,000 research papers, later incorporated into NARCIS.
events.quote: In May 2005, 16 major Dutch universities cooperatively launched DAREnet

events.title: Hwang Woo-suk stem cell papers found fabricated
events.text: Seoul National University announced that Hwang Woo-suk's 2004 and 2005 Science papers on cloned human embryonic stem cells were fabricated. The case also raised concerns about egg donations.
events.quote: The university announced on January 10, 2006, that Hwang's 2004 and 2005 papers in Science were both fabricated.

events.title: Nature trials open peer review
events.text: Nature posted some submitted manuscripts online for signed public comment alongside regular anonymous review; few authors took part.
events.quote: In June 2006, Nature launched an experiment in parallel open peer review

events.title: First CWTS Leiden Ranking
events.text: The first edition of the Leiden Ranking, a university ranking based on bibliometric indicators compiled by CWTS at Leiden University, was produced.
events.quote: The first edition of the Leiden Ranking was produced in 2007.

events.title: US FDA Amendments Act mandates trial registration
events.text: The US FDA Amendments Act made registration of applicable trials on ClinicalTrials.gov mandatory, required results reporting and set penalties for non-compliance.
events.quote: Bush signed the Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act of 2007 (FDAAA) on September 27, 2007.

events.title: STROBE reporting guideline published
events.text: The STROBE checklist for reporting observational studies in epidemiology was published simultaneously in several leading biomedical journals.
events.quote: It was published simultaneously in several leading biomedical journals in October and November 2007

events.title: Beall's List of predatory publishers
events.text: Librarian Jeffrey Beall kept a list of open access publishers he judged predatory, until he removed it in January 2017.
events.quote: Originally started as a personal endeavor in 2008

events.title: EQUATOR Network launched
events.text: The EQUATOR Network, which collects and promotes reporting guidelines such as CONSORT, STARD and TRIPOD, was formally launched in London.
events.quote: The EQUATOR Network was formally launched on 26 June 2008 at the Royal Society of Medicine in London, UK.

events.title: Declaration of Helsinki requires trial registration
events.text: The revised Declaration of Helsinki stated that every clinical trial must be registered in a publicly accessible database before the first participant is recruited.
events.quote: Released in October 2008, the revised Declaration of Helsinki

events.title: PRISMA reporting guideline for meta-analyses
events.text: The QUOROM guideline was updated and renamed PRISMA, the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses.
events.quote: In 2009, QUOROM was updated to address several conceptual and practical advances in the science of systematic reviews

events.title: DataCite founded
events.text: Organisations from six countries, including TU Delft Library, founded DataCite to register persistent identifiers for research data.
events.quote: DataCite was subsequently founded in London on 1 December 2009

events.title: COMET initiative for core outcome sets
events.text: The COMET initiative was launched to support groups developing core outcome sets, agreed minimum outcomes to measure and report in trials.
events.quote: COMET was first launched in 2010

events.title: Unpublished reboxetine trial data revealed
events.text: Germany's IQWiG published a meta-analysis including data on about 3,000 participants that Pfizer had not published, concluding reboxetine was ineffective and potentially harmful.
events.quote: In 2010, the German Institute for Quality and Efficiency in Health Care (IQEHC) published results of a meta-analysis of clinical trial data for reboxetine in acute depression

events.title: Singapore Statement on Research Integrity
events.text: The Singapore Statement on Research Integrity was issued as one of the major international texts on responsible conduct of research.
events.quote: the Singapore Statement on Research Integrity (2010)

events.title: Andrew Wakefield struck off medical register
events.text: Andrew Wakefield was struck off the British medical register for serious professional misconduct linked to his fraudulent 1998 Lancet paper on the MMR vaccine and autism.
events.quote: he was struck off the British medical register in 2010

events.title: Term altmetrics proposed
events.text: The term altmetrics was proposed for measures of research impact based on online and social media attention, as a generalisation of article-level metrics.
events.quote: The term altmetrics was proposed in 2010

events.title: Panton Principles for open data
events.text: Principles stating that published scientific data should be openly available were launched after being drafted in Cambridge in 2009.
events.quote: officially launched in February 2010

events.title: Retraction Watch blog launched
events.text: Science writers Ivan Oransky and Adam Marcus launched Retraction Watch, a blog reporting on retractions; it later built a database of retracted papers.
events.quote: The blog was launched in August 2010

events.title: Bem's 'Feeling the Future' precognition paper
events.text: Daryl Bem reported statistical evidence for precognition in a leading psychology journal; criticism, including Bayes factor reanalyses, fuelled debate about common research practices.
events.quote: In 2011, Bem published the article

events.title: Bayer reports low replication of findings
events.text: An analysis by researchers at Bayer found that, at most, a quarter of the company's in-house findings replicated the original published results.
events.quote: A 2011 analysis by researchers with pharmaceutical company Bayer found that, at most, a quarter of Bayer's in-house findings replicated the original results.

events.title: Sci-Hub founded
events.text: Alexandra Elbakyan started Sci-Hub, a site that gives free access to paywalled research papers regardless of copyright.
events.quote: Sci-Hub was founded in Kazakhstan by Alexandra Elbakyan in 2011

events.title: Dutch H5N1 study sparks dual-use debate
events.text: Plans by Dutch researchers to publish how they made a transmissible H5N1 flu strain raised debate on whether some research data should be withheld.
events.quote: In 2011, Dutch researchers announced their intention to publish a research paper in the journal Science

events.title: European Code of Conduct for Research Integrity
events.text: The European Code of Conduct for Research Integrity was published in 2011 and revised in 2017, setting shared principles for research integrity in Europe.
events.quote: The European Code of Conduct for Research Integrity, published in 2011 and revised in 2017

events.title: Erasmus MC investigation of Don Poldermans
events.text: An Erasmus MC committee found that cardiologist Don Poldermans committed misconduct in DECREASE trials, including missing written informed consent and fabricated data. He was dismissed.
events.quote: the 2011/2012 investigation

events.title: Tilburg University suspends Diederik Stapel
events.text: Tilburg University suspended social psychologist Diederik Stapel for fabricating data, and announced an investigation of his work.
events.quote: In September 2011, Tilburg University suspended Stapel due to his fabrication of data used in research publications.

events.title: 'False-Positive Psychology' paper published
events.text: Simmons, Nelson and Simonsohn showed how flexible choices in collecting and analysing data can produce false positive results, using a deliberately absurd example.
events.quote: Toevallig werd in oktober 2011 het artikel False Positive Psychology gepubliceerd

events.title: Amgen reports low replication in cancer research
events.text: C. Glenn Begley and Lee Ellis reported that only 11% of 53 preclinical cancer studies had replications that confirmed the original conclusions.
events.quote: In a 2012 paper, C. Glenn Begley, a biotech consultant working at Amgen, and Lee Ellis

events.title: Failures to replicate Bem's psi findings published
events.text: The journal that had published Bem's precognition studies published seven experiments that found no evidence for precognition.
events.quote: In 2012, the same journal that published Bem's original experiments

events.title: Publons launched
events.text: Publons offered researchers a way to record and receive credit for their peer review work; it later became part of Web of Science.
events.quote: It was launched in 2012, bought by Clarivate in 2017 and merged into Web of Science in 2022.

events.title: Google Scholar Citations profiles introduced
events.text: Google Scholar allowed individual scholars to create personal citation profiles and started computing an h-index for them.
events.quote: Google Scholar started computing an h-index in 2012 with the advent of individual Scholar pages.

events.title: The Cost of Knowledge boycott of Elsevier
events.text: Mathematician Timothy Gowers called for a boycott of Elsevier over prices and bundling; thousands of researchers signed a pledge.
events.quote: On 21 January 2012, the mathematician Timothy Gowers called for a boycott of Elsevier

events.title: Dirk Smeesters resigns after fraud finding
events.text: Dirk Smeesters, professor of consumer behaviour at Erasmus University Rotterdam, resigned after being found to have committed scientific fraud; he denied the fraud.
events.quote: Op 25 juni 2012 nam Smeesters ontslag nadat hij betrapt was op het plegen van wetenschapsfraude.

events.title: Final report on the Stapel fraud
events.text: The Levelt, Noort and Drenth committees published their joint report on Stapel's fraud, which also criticised the research culture in which it continued.
events.quote: publiceerden op 28 november 2012 het gezamenlijke eindrapport

events.title: Registered Reports introduced at Cortex
events.text: Christopher Chambers introduced Registered Reports at the journal Cortex: study plans are peer reviewed and accepted before data are collected.
events.quote: introduced at the journal Cortex by Christopher Chambers in 2013

events.title: Helsinki revision calls for sharing all results
events.text: The 2013 revision of the Declaration of Helsinki stressed the need to disseminate research results, including negative and inconclusive studies.
events.quote: The revised declaration of 2013 also highlights the need to disseminate research results, including negative and inconclusive studies

events.title: F1000Research publishes before open review
events.text: F1000Research published articles first and then added signed peer review reports and revised versions as they came in.
events.quote: Starting in 2013 with the launch of F1000Research

events.title: Science investigates paper buying in China
events.text: Science published an investigation of research misconduct in China, including scholars buying pre-written papers from an online catalogue to use as their own.
events.quote: In 2013, Science published an investigation of various kinds of research misconduct in China

events.title: Center for Open Science founded
events.text: Brian Nosek and Jeffrey Spies founded the Center for Open Science, funded mainly by the Laura and John Arnold Foundation.
events.quote: founded the organization in January 2013

events.title: AllTrials campaign launched
events.text: Ben Goldacre, the BMJ, Cochrane and others set up AllTrials, which campaigns for all past and current clinical trials to be registered and reported.
events.quote: In January 2013 Goldacre joined the Cochrane Collaboration, British Medical Journal and others in setting up AllTrials

events.title: Research Data Alliance started
events.text: Research funders from Europe, the United States and Australia started the RDA to build technical and social bridges for sharing data.
events.quote: started in 2013 by the European Commission

events.title: Zenodo repository launched
events.text: CERN and OpenAIRE launched Zenodo, a general repository giving persistent identifiers to papers, datasets and software.
events.quote: Zenodo was launched on 8 May 2013

events.title: San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment
events.text: DORA, which originated at a December 2012 meeting of the American Society for Cell Biology, was published with recommendations against misuse of journal impact factors in assessment.
events.quote: was published on May 13, 2013

events.title: Controlled access to HeLa genome data
events.text: After HeLa genome data were published without the Lacks family's knowledge, the NIH announced a policy of controlled access to the data.
events.quote: On 7 August 2013, NIH director Francis Collins announced a policy of controlled access to the cell line genome

events.title: Bohannon's peer review sting
events.text: Science correspondent John Bohannon sent fake papers with obvious flaws to 304 fee-charging open access journals; about 60% of them accepted the papers.
events.quote: The article and associated data were published in the 4 October 2013 issue of Science as open access.

events.title: bioRxiv preprint server founded
events.text: John Inglis and Richard Sever founded bioRxiv at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory to share biology preprints before peer review.
events.quote: co-founded by John Inglis and Richard Sever in November 2013

events.title: First Registered Reports: special issue of replications
events.text: The first Registered Reports appeared in a special issue of the journal Social Psychology containing preregistered replication studies.
events.quote: The first Registered Reports were published in 2014 in a special issue of Social Psychology containing preregistered replication studies.

events.title: Cochrane review of oseltamivir (Tamiflu)
events.text: A Cochrane review concluded that oseltamivir does not reduce hospitalisations; health agencies and the manufacturer Roche rejected its conclusions.
events.quote: A 2014 Cochrane Review concluded that oseltamivir does not reduce hospitalizations

events.title: FAIR principles formulated in Leiden
events.text: At a workshop at the Lorentz Centre of Leiden University, participants first formulated the FAIR principles for research data.
events.quote: In January 2014, the Lorentz Centre at Leiden University hosted a workshop

events.title: EU Clinical Trials Regulation adopted
events.text: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 replaced the Clinical Trials Directive with one directly applicable set of EU rules; it took effect in January 2022.
events.quote: This Directive was repealed by Regulation 536/2014, dated 16 April 2014, which took effect on January 31st, 2022.

events.title: Statcheck developed in the Netherlands
events.text: Michèle Nuijten (Tilburg University) and Sacha Epskamp (University of Amsterdam) developed statcheck, software that detects inconsistencies in reported statistical results.
events.quote: Statcheck was first developed in 2015 by Michele Nuijten of Tilburg University and Sacha Epskamp of the University of Amsterdam.

events.title: Leiden Manifesto for Research Metrics
events.text: Ten principles to guide research evaluation were published in Nature, formulated by Diana Hicks, Paul Wouters and colleagues at a 2014 conference in Leiden.
events.quote: is a 22 April 2015 published comment in Nature

events.title: Dutch universities threaten Elsevier boycott
events.text: The Association of Universities in the Netherlands threatened a boycott; Elsevier later agreed to make 30% of Dutch articles open access by 2018.
events.quote: In July 2015, the Association of Universities in the Netherlands threatened to boycott Elsevier

events.title: Reproducibility Project: Psychology reports results
events.text: A collaboration coordinated by Brian Nosek repeated 100 psychology studies; 36% of replications of significant findings were significant, with effects about half as large.
events.quote: In August 2015, the first open empirical study of reproducibility in psychology was published

events.title: Study 329 reanalysed
events.text: The BMJ published a reanalysis of Study 329, the paroxetine trial in adolescents whose original 2001 report had been ghostwritten and made false efficacy claims.
events.quote: In September 2015 the BMJ published a re-analysis of the study.

events.title: American Statistical Association statement on p-values
events.text: The ASA issued a formal statement that p-values do not measure the probability that a hypothesis is true, nor the size or importance of an effect.
events.quote: In 2016, the American Statistical Association (ASA) made a formal statement

events.title: Multi-lab replication finds no ego depletion
events.text: A replication study with 2,141 participants in about two dozen labs, using a single protocol, found no evidence for the ego depletion effect.
events.quote: In 2016, a major multi-lab replication study (2141 participants) carried out at two dozen labs across the world using a single protocol failed to find any evidence for ego depletion.

events.title: Facial feedback study fails to replicate
events.text: A Registered Replication Report in 17 labs, coordinated by Eric-Jan Wagenmakers (University of Amsterdam), did not reproduce a 1988 facial feedback experiment.
events.quote: In 2016, a large-scale Registered Replication Report was conducted with the purpose of meticulously replicating Strack, Martin, and Stepper's study

events.title: Lead author abandons power posing
events.text: After several failed replications, Dana Carney, lead author of the original 2010 power posing paper, issued a statement abandoning the theory.
events.quote: in 2016, Carney issued a statement abandoning the theory

events.title: FAIR Guiding Principles published
events.text: After refinement by a FORCE11 working group, the FAIR principles for findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable data were published in Scientific Data.
events.quote: They were published in the March 2016 issue of Scientific Data.

events.title: Amsterdam Call for Action on Open Science
events.text: During the Dutch EU Presidency, a conference in Amsterdam presented a call for concrete steps towards open science in Europe.
events.quote: The Dutch Presidency of the Council of the European Union called out for action in April 2016

events.title: EU adopts the GDPR
events.text: The European Union adopted the General Data Protection Regulation, which took effect in May 2018 and governs the processing of personal data.
events.quote: adopted the GDPR on 14 April 2016

events.title: Society for the Improvement of Psychological Science founded
events.text: The Society for the Improvement of Psychological Science (SIPS) was founded at its first meeting, held at the Center for Open Science in Charlottesville.
events.quote: It was founded at its inaugural meeting that took place June 6-8th, 2016 at Center for Open Science in Charlottesville.

events.title: NWO funds replication studies
events.text: The Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research (NWO) made 3 million euro available for replication studies in social sciences, health research and healthcare innovation.
events.quote: In July 2016, the Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research made €3 million available for replication studies.

events.title: Proposal to redefine significance as p < 0.005
events.text: A group of 72 authors proposed lowering the threshold for statistical significance from 0.05 to 0.005; others proposed justifying thresholds before collecting data instead.
events.quote: In 2017, a group of 72 authors proposed to enhance reproducibility by changing the p-value threshold

events.title: GO FAIR office established
events.text: Germany, the Netherlands and France agreed to set up an international office to support putting the FAIR principles into practice.
events.quote: In 2017, Germany, Netherlands and France agreed to establish

events.title: PREreview platform launched
events.text: PREreview was launched to train and involve early-career and underrepresented researchers in open peer review of preprints.
events.quote: In 2017, the platform PREreview was launched

events.title: Nature and Science social science papers replicated
events.text: A project replicated 21 social and behavioural science papers published in Nature and Science; about 62% reproduced the original results.
events.quote: A study published in 2018 in Nature Human Behaviour replicated 21 social and behavioral science papers from Nature and Science

events.title: Plan S launched
events.text: Eleven research funders, including the Dutch Research Council (NWO), launched Plan S, requiring research they fund to be freely accessible immediately from 2020.
events.quote: In september 2018 lanceerden 11 fondsen voor wetenschappelijk onderzoek, waaronder de Nederlandse Organisatie voor Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek

events.title: European Open Science Cloud launched
events.text: The European Commission's EOSC, started in 2015, officially launched with a portal giving access to research services.
events.quote: The European Open Science Cloud officially launched in November 2018

events.title: Dutch recognition and rewards system announced
events.text: Dutch universities and research funders announced a new system of research recognition and reward based on the DORA principles.
events.quote: In November 2019, Dutch universities and research funders announced the introduction of a new system of research recognition and reward, based on the DORA principles.

events.title: Dutch transformative agreement with Elsevier
events.text: Dutch research organisations signed a four-year transformative agreement with the publisher Elsevier.
events.quote: In 2020, the Dutch research organised signed a four year transformative agreement with publishers Elsevier.

events.title: Bik identifies hundreds of paper-mill articles
events.text: Science reported that Elisabeth Bik had identified over 400 papers published in China that apparently all came from the same paper mill company.
events.quote: In February 2020, Science reported that Bik had identified over 400 research papers published in China

events.title: Springer Nature signs DORA
events.text: Springer Nature became the largest research publisher to sign the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment.
events.quote: On 20 May 2020 Springer Nature became the largest research publisher to sign the declaration.

events.title: Hong Kong Principles for assessing researchers
events.text: The Hong Kong Principles for assessing researchers were adopted, naming open science as one of five pillars of research integrity to reward in assessment.
events.quote: First adopted in July 2020, the Hong Kong principles for assessing researchers

events.title: Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology reports
events.text: The project examined 193 experiments from 53 top cancer papers; replicated effect sizes were on average 85% smaller than in the original papers.
events.quote: In 2021, the project showed that of 193 experiments from 53 top papers about cancer

events.title: Nature reports thousands of paper-mill papers
events.text: A report in Nature stated that thousands of journal papers had been traced to paper mills, and some journals were revising their review processes.
events.quote: According to a 2021 report in Nature, thousands of papers in academic journals had been traced to paper mills

events.title: Utrecht University drops impact factor
events.text: Utrecht University announced it would no longer use the journal impact factor in hiring and promotion decisions, partly inspired by DORA.
events.quote: In June 2021, Utrecht University announced that it would no longer use the impact factor in hiring and promotion decisions.

events.title: UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science
events.text: UNESCO member states adopted the first international standard-setting instrument on open science, which is not legally binding.
events.quote: The Recommendation was adopted at the 41st session of the General Conference on 23 November 2021

events.title: AI-generated Western blot images flagged
events.text: At the European Hematology Association Congress, Elisabeth Bik presented information about artificial intelligence being used to fraudulently generate Western blot images.
events.quote: During a session of the 2022 European Hematology Association Congress, Bik presented information about artificial intelligence being used to fraudulently generate Western blot images.

events.title: eLife drops accept/reject decisions
events.text: eLife announced it would publish all reviewed papers as preprints with public reviews and an assessment, instead of accepting or rejecting them.
events.quote: On October 20, 2022, eLife announced

events.title: ChatGPT released
events.text: OpenAI released ChatGPT, a chatbot based on a large language model whose capabilities were described at the time as unprecedented.
events.quote: The original version of ChatGPT, released in November 2022

events.title: Large preregistered replication finds no precognition
events.text: A large preregistered replication, designed together with Bem and other proponents of extrasensory perception, found no evidence for precognition.
events.quote: A large-scale pre-registered replication in 2023

events.title: ChatGPT listed as co-author on papers
events.text: Nature reported that at least four preprints or papers had listed ChatGPT as a co-author; Nature and JAMA Network prohibit listing a chatbot as co-author.
events.quote: In January 2023, Nature reported that at least four academic preprints or published papers had listed ChatGPT as a co-author.

events.title: AI-generated figures in retracted Frontiers paper
events.text: A paper in Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology, later retracted, was criticised for figures generated with the image tool Midjourney.
events.quote: A now-retracted 2024 paper published in Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology was criticized for having figures AI generated with Midjourney

events.title: Harvard finds Francesca Gino falsified data
events.text: A Harvard Business School committee found that Francesca Gino had falsified data in four published studies, after problems were raised by the Data Colada bloggers.
events.quote: In March 2024, Harvard Business School's investigative committee

events.title: Wiley retracts papers linked to Hindawi
events.text: The Wall Street Journal reported that more than 11,300 papers were retracted and 19 journals closed after fake studies affected Wiley's Hindawi journals.
events.quote: In May 2024, the Wall Street Journal published a report on fake studies that affected New Jersey publisher Wiley.

events.title: CONSORT 2025 statement
events.text: The CONSORT group issued an updated checklist replacing the 2010 version, adding an open-science section on trial registration, protocol access and data sharing.
events.quote: In April 2025 the CONSORT group issued an updated 'CONSORT 2025' checklist

events.title: SCORE project reports replicability of social science
events.text: The SCORE project studied 3,900 social-science papers published between 2009 and 2018 and found that only about half of the results could be replicated.
events.quote: In 2026, the SCORE Project study of 3,900 social-science papers between 2009 and 2018 found that only about half the results could be replicated.
